**One star until Stackhouse fixes our migration and answers for its support**

Bridger Bend Community Library has one branch, two full-time staff members plus volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year Stackhouse Cloud contract in June 2026 at $14,200 per year and went live on October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped, taking roughly 640 holds with it. Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, all saying the issue was “escalated to engineering,” while our volunteer records checkouts on index cards like it’s 1975.

This has real consequences for our patrons. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to collect his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and had to send him home with nothing.

Our sales representative promised “a dedicated migration specialist.” What we got was a shared inbox. To be fair, the software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is genuinely better than our old system. The problem is not the product idea. It is the lack of effective support when a migration goes wrong.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and this line item is on the agenda. I need to be able to explain to our commissioners what Stackhouse is doing to fix this.

What I am asking for is straightforward: a named person at Stackhouse must call me this week, take ownership of our case, and provide a concrete recovery plan and timeline. We need working circulation, an explanation of what happened to our holds data, and a clear answer about what can be restored.

I am giving Stackhouse one star for now and will revisit that rating if the company resolves these problems. Meanwhile, I urge directors at other small libraries to get support response times, escalation procedures, and migration staffing commitments in writing before signing. Ask who will answer when your library is down—not who will demonstrate the software before you buy it.
